- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.7) and model shows flat or slow rise, adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to capture momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.
- If official event net is heavily bearish (bearish > bullish by 20+), model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% downward bias to 30d forecast.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.0 to 1.0 or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
- If supply net is negative and events are frequent, model tends to overestimate price; reduce forecast by 1–3% per event cluster.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak, price drops >10%), model often fails to revert; add 1–3% downward correction after peak.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0–0.5), model often overestimates upside; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average.
